 Drake Maye's value will be crystal clear during absence from Patriots
 Any and all potential for the Patriots to have a productive season was hanging by a thread, even before the team flew to Germany earlier in the week. Pulling out a win against the Lions, defending home turf against the Vikings and Broncos, and the Patriots had a chance to get to 10 wins, earn a spot in the postseason, and complete a decent season amid a near-comical number of key injuries up and down the roster.
 But then, Drake Maye quietly walked to the locker room in Munich, taking any and all hopes for the season with him.
 Of course, head coach Mike Vrabel will try to spin things positive during what looks like a season-long absence for his quarterback, because admitting it's over before Thanksgiving won't exactly boost morale in the locker room.
 But Vrabel knows. Josh McDaniels knows. Every player on the team, from A.J. Brown to long snapper Julian Ashby? They know, too.
 The 2026 Patriots are done.
 That's not a ground-shaking statement, of course, as very few teams can withstand the loss of their starting quarterback. It's both interesting and unfortunate, though, because everybody on the inside and the outside of the organization is about to learn just how valuable Maye is to the franchise.
 Even in the small sample of Sunday's game, it was evident. 
 Maye played five and a half minutes of the game against the Lions. He was 3-for-4 for 48 yards (the incompletion was a throwaway) and he ran once for 11 yards, contributing 59 yards of offense for the Patriots.
 With Tommy DeVito at QB, the offense gained nine yards -- nine yards -- over the Patriots' next eight offensive drives.
 The Patriots finished the game with just 151 yards of offense, with 70 of those yards -- over 46 percent -- coming on that one drive with Maye.
 Could it be better with DeVito -- or Behren Morton, for that matter -- taking reps as the starter with proper preparation for an opponent? Sure. It kind of has to. DeVito had a negative-0.56 EPA per dropback and a negative-12.5 completion percentage over expected. His overall EPA was negative-17.3.
 Drake Maye still owns the best single-game EPA this season (28.7, vs. the Raiders). DeVito now has the 14th-worst single-game EPA this season (of QBs with at least 30 dropbacks). And that was against a defense that entered Sunday with the 32nd-ranked pass defense in terms of yards and touchdowns allowed per game.
 Roger McCreary picks it off! pic.twitter.com/fnJ3pI69vw 
— Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 15, 2026 
 It technically could get worse for DeVito and the offense, but even if it improves, it will only be incrementally.
 And that will, with great certainty, display just how valuable Maye has been for this offense over the past two years. 
 Such a thing shouldn't really be a matter of debate, even with Maye's rise in interceptions this year. Yet whether it's because Maye isn't perfect , or because we can't get enough when it comes to nitpicking and criticizing quarterbacks, there's unquestionably been plenty of such conversation, ranging from gentle criticism to outright anti-Maye slander.
 And while the defense has rightfully found itself under the microscope after two absolute thrashings from the Packers and Lions, that unit will have absolutely no shot at stopping anybody if the Patriots' offense keeps putting the defense back on the field in a lifeless stretch of three-and-outs.
 Give it another week or two, and nobody will be able to doubt how valuable Maye has been for this team -- the entire team -- over the past two seasons. A rocky road lies ahead.

 Neemias Queta OUT vs. Magic
 The Celtics listed Neemias Queta as questionable for tonight's game due to rest, but he's officially OUT for the game.
 Queta only played 15 minutes on Sunday but has played every game thus far for the C's, starting the last eight.
 Joe Mazzulla will likely put Mitchell Robinson back into the starting lineup, where he was for the first five games of the season.

 One Possession: Jordan Walsh brings some historic energy
 The Boston Celtics were putting together a historic first quarter on Sunday night against the Dallas Mavericks and Jordan Walsh’s emphatic first pump and scream told the story of how they did it. 
 Walsh had just swiped an errant pass and broke in alone against Mavs young superstar Cooper Flagg. Walsh went right at the 19-year-old, then finished a layup while getting hacked from behind by Caleb Martin. It was the second straight and-1 finish for Walsh, who emphatically pumped his fist and screamed as teammates rushed to celebrate with him.
 View this post on Instagram 
 Walsh put up eight points on 3-of-5 shooting over 5:48 during his first shift of the game. The Celtics outscored the Mavericks by 18 in his floor time. The Mavericks generated just two field goals as a team for the entirety of the first frame and Boston set a franchise record while outscoring them 42-9 overall. 
 We’d make the case that Walsh’s energy out of the gates was a big reason Boston put the game on cruise control against a Dallas team limping through its third game in four nights. 
 Walsh has now started eight games for the Celtics this season, easily the most among any of the team’s deep collection of wings (Hugo Gonzalez has three starts, Baylor Scheierman two, Sam Hauser one). Eyebrows went skyward when head coach Joe Mazzulla slotted Walsh in Boston’s starting lineup to start the preseason but Walsh has largely stuck in that role.
 And it’s the growing offensive confidence that might keep him there.
 On Sunday night, Walsh didn’t hesitate when the ball swung his way early for open looks beyond the 3-point arc. Mazzulla even thrust his arm in the air on each of Walsh’s first two no-hesitation attempts. The first slammed off the rim but Walsh made the next. He went into attack mode soon after drawing the consecutive and-1 finishes.
 The Celtics are outscoring opponents by 5.8 points per 100 possessions during Walsh’s 215 minutes of floor time. It’s the second lowest mark among regulars, trailed only by Mitchell Robinson (-3.9 net rating in 212 minutes). And it admittedly doesn’t pop the way that someone like Hauser (+22.4) or Scheierman (+13.5) has given the way Boston’s bench has dominated their minutes.
 But it’s not hard to understand why Walsh is getting his opportunity with the starting group. His willingness to defend a top scorer on the opposing team is a luxury that takes stress off veterans like Paul George and Jayson Tatum. Just look at the numbers from some of Walsh’s most frequent matchups through the early portion of the 2026-27 season:
 Walsh's challenge, however, is staying aggressive on the offensive end, even when sharing the floor with elite scorers like George and Tatum. Teams are naturally going to expend most of their energy on those All-Stars, which means Walsh is going to get a bunch of open looks.
 In the past, he might hesitate on shots. He would get timid after missing an early attempt. On Sunday night, he hoisted the ball with confidence. He didn’t look to give up the ball in transition, he went right at Flagg despite half the building seemingly trekking down from Maine to see their native son.
 That’s the version of Walsh the Celtics need. That’s the version of Walsh that can stick in the starting lineup. That’s the Walsh that fueled Boston’s historic first quarter.
